absent: Locking, ownership and concurrency rules for rpc request and XDR stream objects.
Allocation, lifetime and error recovery for streams, scratch storage, folios and generated variable-length buffers.
Wire layout and alignment details beyond remaining, padding and opaque count-plus-payload sizing.
State machine or sequencing constraints across successive encode and decode calls.
Meaning of NFSv4 status, attribute, delegation, ACL and notify values beyond their identity as constants.
Behavior of cross-dossier reservation, inline-window, commit, conversion and hyper helpers.

findings.text: Provides a kernel RPC decode callback type that consumes a request descriptor plus a byte stream and reports an integer status.
Provides scratch area management for an XDR stream: install caller buffer, install whole folio contents, clear to empty, and flush pending scratch data only when nonempty.

Provides inline encoders for optional-item marker, boolean, host-order 32-bit, already network-order 32-bit, 64-bit, counted opaque bytes with inline and copying forms, and counted host-order 32-bit vector.

Provides inline decoders and testers for boolean, 32-bit host and network forms, 64-bit, counted opaque with caller limit and inline pointer, and counted 32-bit vector, plus present versus absent testers on one wire unit.

Encode path reserves wire space first and fails when unavailable; success reports the wire length consumed while reservation failure reports message-too-large and, for inline opaque, also clears the caller pointer.

Decode path obtains an inline window first; missing or truncated data reports bad-message, while oversize opaque or oversize vector relative to caller capacity reports message-too-large. Scalar decoders report zero on success.

Wire booleans and optional-item markers share one false and one true network word: absent and false use the zero word and present and nonzero use the one word; presence means not equal to the zero word.
Stream accounting treats remaining length as stored word count scaled to bytes, padding as aligned size minus true size, and opaque wire size as one count word plus aligned payload.
Generic generated-XDR vocabulary: boolean aliases, length plus byte-pointer string and opaque records, and counted arrays expressed as count plus element pointer for bitmaps, paths, and ACL lists.

NFSv4.1 core records: time as seconds plus nanoseconds, attributes as mask plus value blob, state identifier as sequence plus twelve opaque bytes, share/open claim/create-mode argument bundle, POSIX ACL entry as tag plus permission plus identity, and delegation-change timestamps.

Directory delegation notification records: per-file entry pairing name and attributes, cookie-linked predecessor, remove and multi-part add forms, attribute-only and rename wrappers, cookie-verifier change pair, mask plus opaque value notification, and callback arguments carrying state, handle and change list with a status-only reply.

XDR sizing vocabulary: one wire unit for void-equivalent, boolean, short, integer and long widths, two units for 64-bit widths, and per-type NFSv4 size formulas built from count words, quad lengths, and nested member sizes.

NFSv4.1 fixed sizes and attribute numbers: eight-byte verifier, 128-unit file-handle bound, and attribute identifiers for offline, delegation times, open arguments, ACL true form and scope, and POSIX default and access ACLs.

NFSv4.1 status and option enumerations: success plus low POSIX-like codes and a large 10001-and-above NFS4-specific range, share access and deny values, delegation and claim and create-mode selectors, open share-want masks, POSIX permission bits, ACL model and scope, and directory-notification reason codes.

Variable-length decoding validates before exposing pointers: opaque decode initializes the out-pointer, enforces caller maximum after checking availability, and returns payload length with no pointer for zero length; vector decode guards count multiplication overflow, supports size query with null destination, zero-fills short vectors, and still converts the fitting prefix when too large.
